productionAudit: ByteTransport.onData -> Connection.#handleData -> ServerMessageDecoder/FrameDecoder -> CBOR decode + TypeBox validation -> Connection.#handleMessage -> PiClient.#handleMessage -> ClientState.applyEvent/revision gates/#notify -> lease subscription callback. User listeners are outside the internal allocation claim.

Complete frame/decode/validation creates byte views or copies for fragmented input, decoded records/arrays/strings, validator Sets, and iterable machinery. Sampling includes these pre-existing allocations; this path is not globally allocation-free.

Client event dispatch adds a primitive lifecycle ID check per decoded message; response dispatch checks pending session identity/generation before applying state. ClientState avoids an empty fallback listener array.

Explicit connect/handshake/request/acquire/lease/release/reconciliation/dispose boundaries own existing async promises, callbacks and maps. Added generation fields are primitives on existing lease/request records. No new periodic timer, object pool, replay queue or persistent event log.

Server SessionManager acquire/attach/runOperation/runtime-event/disconnect/maybeDispose were audited. Busy runtime stays server-owned; idle unowned runtime can be disposed. No coding-agent service adapter is supplied by this experimental core; durable background-task completion is not claimed.
capacityAndOwnership: Existing frame payload default 16 MiB, decode depth 64 / collection entries 1,000,000; ordered transport must bound its outbound queue. Complete-frame fixture adds no outbound backlog, partial frame, replay cursor or replay pages.

Pending requests and lease/attachment/reconciliation maps retain the existing per-request/per-session ownership model. Disconnect clears pending lifecycle maps, rejects pending requests and invalidates leases; per-session removal clears its lifecycle entries. No new entry capacity is claimed.
Existing numeric session-generation tombstones remain per observed removed/invalidated session ID for the PiClient lifetime; this change does not introduce a bounded historical-ID cache.

Snapshot cache is intentionally retained across disconnect for offline inspection; connect resets it and dispose clears it. Fresh attach forgets prior revision before accepting the authoritative snapshot.

Lease subscriptions remain registered until explicit unsubscribe or client.dispose, even after detach/disconnect. Invalid leases suppress snapshot delivery. WeakRef fixture calls final client.dispose, holds owner objects strongly, yields then forces GC eight times; it proves release at these boundaries, not immediate unsubscribe on disconnect.

Invalidated leases cannot revive or release replacement ownership. Normal last-owner detach, failed detach retry, failed dispose reconciliation, session removal and explicit disconnection/transport failure are covered by behavior tests; no OS process or daemon cancellation claim.
